messages:
sam: quick note — saw multiple new users fail our sample app because the env var name differs across SDKs. go expects REDWOOD_API_KEY, python still accepts REDWOOD_KEY. onboarding hit rate up 7%.
anya: ouch. do we know which sample apps ship the old name?
sam: the flask sample and the cli quickstart still use REDWOOD_KEY in README. go/sdk and js/sdk already read REDWOOD_API_KEY.
kevin: thats a bad first impression. proposal: normalize on REDWOOD_API_KEY, emit a one-time deprecation warning if REDWOOD_KEY is present, and support a 6mo deprecation window. add a migration note in quickstarts.
maria: agree. also we should avoid relying only on env vars for org/project scoping. people paste keys tied to orgs but then wonder why route defaults wrong.
jon: suggestion: support explicit REDWOOD_ORG_ID and REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID env vars, but keep legacy behavior where keys can be prefixed like "org:proj:<key>". CLI should parse that when present.
anya: +1 on explicit vars. can we also have the SDK merge precedence: CLI config > explicit env vars > embedded key prefix > SDK default? documentable list.
kevin: yes. precedence order is important for platform teams. I'll draft the order in the SDK spec and PRs for go/python/js.
sam: implementation detail for the deprecation warning: emit it exactly once per process and attach a metric so we can track how many warn events are firing. minimal noise.
maria: for rotation — instead of long-lived API keys, we should add optional short-lived session tokens and refresh flow. i.e., rw login issues a session token stored in ~/.redwood/credentials and SDK auto-refreshes via refresh token.
jon: that will help customers that need key revocation without touching infra secrets. rollout idea: implement session tokens in CLI + go/js sdks first, then python. session tokens should have ttl 1h by default and refreshable up to 30d with a refresh token.
kevin: parity note: js/go currently have a simple env detection helper. python version needs to match behavior: same env names, same precedence, same deprecation message. otherwise sample apps will continue to confuse.
anya: sample app checklist for this work: update README env names, add migration notice, add interactive rw login docs, add code snippet showing fallback detection, and include a short snippet for k8s secrets examples.
sam: code snippet we can use in SDKs for the one-time warn:
```
if os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'):
    key = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
elif os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'):
    key = os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')
    warn_once('REDWOOD_KEY is deprecated; set REDWOOD_API_KEY instead')
else:
    key = None
```
maria: small UX ask — CLI should print a single migration hint on login if it finds REDWOOD_KEY in the environment: "Detected legacy REDWOOD_KEY. Run `rw migrate-keys` or set REDWOOD_API_KEY." include a link to the migration doc.
kevin: timeline proposal: draft docs + python PR this week, CLI changes next sprint, rollout deprecation notices for 6 months, hard remove after that unless major pushback.
jon: tests: add unit tests for precedence, deprecation warning, and session token refresh in each SDK. add integration test that runs the flask sample with the new env names.
anya: can someone own updating internal quickstarts? currently blocking onboarding flow improvements.
sam: i'll pick quickstarts and coordinate with kevin on SDK PRs.
kevin: assigning myself to python SDK parity PR. will follow the warning format used in go.
dev-bot: new release detected: cli v0.34.0 published — please schedule a patch release once python PR lands.
maria: thanks all. i'll start the migration doc draft and list recommended k8s secret patterns.
jon: one last note — telemetry event name: auth_env_deprecation_warn. store a hashed key fingerprint, not the key itself. privacy ok.
sam: perfect. i'll open a tracking ticket and link it to the PRs.
kevin: will post PR link here when ready.
